reason: A scale or bract 'with a flower' subtends a flower; that is a relation to another part, not a quality, and the flower is not part of the bract, so it cannot be entity presence.
Ascidiform means pitcher-shaped. FLOPO:0991104 urceolate is defined as shaped like an urn or pitcher: swollen below and contracted at the mouth.
A 'corklike margin' of the fruit is a corky margin; the margin is the bearer.
A compound of two margin values, PATO entire and FLOPO:0991113 sinuate, read as a continuum between them.
'Forklike pubescent' means the hairs are forked. The quality is bifurcated and its bearer is the hair, trichome (PO_0000282), not the leaf.
Not prophyllate means without a prophyll at the base of the inflorescence.
Branches that radiate from a common point fit FLOPO:0991272 (segments radiating from a common point). This holds for tubers, rhizomes and stigmas alike.

target: new: conjunction of two surface values
reason: Two surface qualities held together, PATO_0001512 punctate and FLOPO:0991059 papillose. It is not a continuum and needs no new term.
The word names a part, the secondary axes, whose length is measured with PATO length. PO_0009081 covers the inflorescence branches without fixing which order 'secondary' means.
Stiltlike roots are stilt roots, i.e. supporting prop roots. The PO lexicon also lists 'stilt root' as a synonym of shoot-borne root (PO_0000042), its parent.
A compound of obovate and cuneate, with the approximating 'sub-' on the first value.
Margins of leaflets, pinnae or fruit 'without spines' are not spiny. PO has no general spine class, only spine leaf, spine stipule and spine petiole.

target: new: outline with apex modifier (split into outline ovate + apex acuminate)
reason: It combines two attributes, an ovate outline (FLOPO:0991024) and an acuminate apex. It should become two statements, not a term.

label: agamosporous
definition: A reproductive quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its producing unreduced spores whose gametophytes give rise to sporophytes without fertilization.
reason: A standard fern reproductive character used in keys. PATO has only the general reproductive quality.
The adverbial form of FLOPO:0991245 anadromous, whose listed bearers include the vein (PO_0005020).
In fern pinnae, anisomerous means unequal-sided about the costa (the acroscopic half is larger), i.e. asymmetrical. The floral sense, unequal numbers of parts per whorl, does not apply to pinnae.
Argenteous means silvery. The colour synonyms map silver and silvery to FLOPO:0988009 white (RELATED), since lustre is not a colour.
Belt-shaped means long, narrow and parallel-sided, i.e. lorate or strap-shaped.
An outline widest at the middle and narrowing to both ends is elliptic. FLOPO:0991024 ovate is the counterpart for 'broadest below the middle'.

label: centripetal
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its flowers developing and opening in sequence from the base or periphery towards the apex or centre.
reason: The order in which an inflorescence's flowers develop is a real botanical character, and neither PATO nor FLOPO has a term for it. The opposite would be centrifugal.

target: new: extent of fusion (connate to a level)
reason: The quality is FLOPO:0991067 connate. 'To below the middle' gives the extent of fusion, which belongs in the record, not in a new term.
The corky spots on pome fruits and hypanthia (Rosaceae) are lenticels, so corky-spotted reads like lenticellate.
A transcription fragment. The covering, 'hoodlike projections', was cut off.
A fragment that has lost its noun, presumably bullate scales. 'Covered' needs what does the covering, and bullate already exists as FLOPO:0991122.
This is a part (cystoliths) with its colour and shape, not a quality word. PO has no cystolith class to state its presence.
A compound of two apex values, cuspidate and caudate, read as a continuum.
A panicle-like inflorescence with cymose branches is a thyrse. FLOPO:0991199 is defined as having an indeterminate main axis and cymose lateral branches.
Dauciform means carrot-shaped: a root tapering evenly downwards from a broad top, i.e. conical. Napiform (FLOPO:0991306) narrows abruptly and is the turnip shape.
Dictyogenous monocot leaves and veins (Smilax, Dioscorea type) have net venation, which is FLOPO:0991100 reticulate.
Stamens differing in size means a set of like parts whose members differ in size, which is the definition of FLOPO:0991101 unequal.
